tickets.title: The Decision API picks entries from an owner pool for a role's job
tickets.what: Spec §2.2 (Decision API uses, D-2026-11-24-04). A role file may declare `"pool": {"dir": "<abs path>", "max": 4, "default": ["<file>.md", ...]}` (first user: frontend-imp pointing at the owner's Personal Standards style pool; HUD reads it, owns none of it). On hud_create for that role: build an index of the pool (each `*.md` except README.md: file name, `# ` title, and the header lines before the first `## `, at most 400 bytes per entry; plus the first 8 KiB of README.md as selection rules; bounded to 64 entries / 48 KiB). If the brief already names any entry by file name or stem, make no call and record that. Otherwise, when the new Settings switch `poolPick` (Decision API group, default on) is on, call the Decision API the way `src/mcp/sonic-thinking.ts` does (brief as untrusted quoted data, first 4000 chars) for 1..max entry file names plus a one-line reason; drop unknown names. On switch off, failure or timeout, use `default`. Attach the picked files as references exactly like context_files (a read line for local workers, bounded inline for browser roles). Record `pool_pick {entries, reason, source: 'decision'|'brief'|'default', ms}` on the job record and the archive, and show it in the hud_create receipt so the main session can tell the owner in one line. Same timeout and fallback discipline as Sonic thinking; no call for roles without `pool`.

acceptance.text: A fixture pool and a brief with no entry named produce a Decision API request listing the entries (stubbed endpoint) and attach the returned files; unknown names are dropped
A brief naming an entry makes no call and records source brief; switch off or endpoint failure records source default with the default files
pool_pick appears on job.json, the archive row and the hud_create receipt
docs/reference.md describes the role-file pool field and the Settings switch in one paragraph; the MCP tool declaration budget test still passes

tickets.title: Pool pick may attach nothing when the work already has an art direction
tickets.what: Owner 2026-11-24: when a mature art direction already exists, the pick must be able to attach nothing; design its inputs, outputs and handling so it is dependable. Change pool-pick/01 as follows. Deterministic steps first, no model call: (1) role prewalk off or `poolPick` off: no pick, nothing attached. (2) The brief names pool entries: use them (`source: brief`). (3) The project declares an established look in `.hud/project.json` as `"design": "<repo-relative path>"`: attach that file as a reference instead of pool entries (`source: project`, `need: existing`). Otherwise one Decision API call, fixed choices only. Input: the brief (untrusted quoted data, first 4000 chars), the pool index (file, title, Kind, Status, Fits) and the README rules, plus two facts: the role and the project name (HUD infers nothing else about existing UI). Output choices: `need`: `existing` (the brief changes or extends a UI that already has its own look) or `new` (a new page, app or sample without a look); `kind`: `personal` or `showcase`; then ranked entry slots as in 01 (slot 1 required only when need is new; later slots may be NONE). Handling: need `existing` attaches nothing from the pool. need `new`: drop unknown entries, drop entries whose Kind contradicts the chosen kind (`either` always fits), keep pool order of dimensions; if nothing is left, attach nothing and record why. Decision API off, failing or timing out: attach nothing (`source: failed`); the frontend worker's skill already falls back to its quick default when the brief names no style. Remove the role-file `default` fallback from 01. Record `{type: 'pick', need, kind, entries, source, ms, dropped?}` (in the prewalk list once prewalk/01 lands; until then in `pool_pick`), and show one receipt line, e.g. `pick: none (existing look)` or `pick: personal · layout-swiss-editorial + theme-dark-near-black + colour-on-elements`.

acceptance.text: A stubbed decision answering need existing attaches nothing; need new with a kind-contradicting entry drops it and records it in dropped
A project with `design` in .hud/project.json attaches that file and makes no call; a brief naming entries makes no call
Decision API failure or switch off attaches nothing; the role-file default field is gone from code and docs
The receipt shows the one-line pick summary; docs/reference.md describes need, kind and the project design field
